items.name: Roblox Open Cloud
items.evidence: BLOCKED ON TWO THINGS, AND MY EARLIER WORDING OVERSTATED IT. I wrote "blocked on something that does not exist", which reads as impossible. Checked against the code rather than the note: apps/worker/src/env.ts:42 DOES declare ROBLOX_API_KEY, scope `creator-store-product:read`, documented as free from create.roblox.com/dashboard/credentials and used by assets.ts for Creator Store SEARCH. When unset, search degrades to the unauthenticated endpoint — it is never required. So Open Cloud is not absent; a READ scope is wired and optional. What is missing is (1) an upload-scoped key, which is a different Open Cloud permission, and (2) any code path that calls an upload endpoint — grep finds no apis.roblox.com asset call anywhere in apps/worker/src. Whether an upload scope is obtainable on this account is a Roblox platform question I cannot answer from here, and I am not going to assert it either way twice. This is the primary row for the dependency; f-6cb625cf and f-cc078607 share it.

items.evidence: packages/training/src/contamination.test.mjs — 8 tests, 4 falsifications. shingles and contaminated were unexported until now, so the guard that keeps training data out of the eval set had never been run by a test. An 8-word overlap IS caught wherever it sits; an unrelated example is NOT (the control — a guard returning true for everything would pass the first case and be useless); a 7-word overlap is below the window and is not caught. DOCUMENTED FAIL-OPEN: an EMPTY eval set makes every example clean, so a task directory that moved or failed to parse would disable contamination checking. It is tolerable only because main() prints its denominator, and a test asserts that line still exists — the announcement lives in the caller, not in the guard.

items.name: Export Roblox asset
items.evidence: BLOCKED ON TWO THINGS, AND MY EARLIER WORDING OVERSTATED IT. I wrote "blocked on something that does not exist", which reads as impossible. Checked against the code rather than the note: apps/worker/src/env.ts:42 DOES declare ROBLOX_API_KEY, scope `creator-store-product:read`, documented as free from create.roblox.com/dashboard/credentials and used by assets.ts for Creator Store SEARCH. When unset, search degrades to the unauthenticated endpoint — it is never required. So Open Cloud is not absent; a READ scope is wired and optional. What is missing is (1) an upload-scoped key, which is a different Open Cloud permission, and (2) any code path that calls an upload endpoint — grep finds no apis.roblox.com asset call anywhere in apps/worker/src. Whether an upload scope is obtainable on this account is a Roblox platform question I cannot answer from here, and I am not going to assert it either way twice. Same dependency as f-968b4ca6. Export needs the upload scope and an exporter, neither of which exists.

items.name: Authorization
items.evidence: API BOUNDARY PROVEN; DATABASE-LEVEL RLS NOT. Against the deployed origin: /api/me refuses an unauthenticated caller with HTTP 401 and returns the account for an authenticated one, the providers route sits behind user auth, and a foreign project id is refused. So authorization is enforced at the route layer on production. THE GAP: the row's claim is Postgres RLS in infra/supabase/migrations, and none of the above exercises it. The material is present — 8 tables created, 8 with row level security enabled, 12 policies scoping (select auth.uid()) = owner_id — but reading migrations proves a PRECONDITION, not the property, and is blind to anything changed in the dashboard. Blocked on the docker-backed policy test. Measured by rbxai-1d on the deployed origin, 2026-09-15, via the first invocation in which --no-model has ever done anything (see docs/FAILURES.md F-63). Not re-run by me: §12.5 permits infra/smoke.mjs at most once per pass and it has been used.

items.name: Rate limiting
items.evidence: apps/worker/tests/rate-limit-overflow.test.mjs — 4 tests, 5 falsifications. MEASURED DEFECT, now fixed (91e7f01): one Map held every counter, and the memory bound "if (ipHits.size > 5000) ipHits.clear()" let an UNAUTHENTICATED flood at /api/studio/claim erase the admin-fail lockout. Measured: 121 wrong keys gave 429; a 5,200-address flood then gave 403 with the counter gone and 120 fresh guesses. Now sweeps expired entries and evicts the LEAST ACTIVE, which under a flood is the flood own one-hit entries rather than the counter currently blocking someone. Reintroducing clear() reddens the finding test and only that test.

items.name: Tenant isolation
items.evidence: API BOUNDARY PROVEN; DATABASE-LEVEL RLS NOT. A signed-in account requesting a project id it does not own gets HTTP 404 from the deployed worker — and 404 rather than 403 is the part worth having, because 403 would distinguish "exists but forbidden" from "no such thing" and leak the existence of other tenants' projects by status code alone. THE GAP: this is one account, one foreign id, one route. It says nothing about whether the Postgres RLS policies hold for every table, nor whether a direct PostgREST call carrying a user JWT is constrained — which is the half the docker-backed policy test exists for and which has never run. Blocked on that test, which needs a local two-tenant Postgres and therefore the owner's decision on starting Docker. Measured by rbxai-1d on the deployed origin, 2026-09-15, via the first invocation in which --no-model has ever done anything (see docs/FAILURES.md F-63). Not re-run by me: §12.5 permits infra/smoke.mjs at most once per pass and it has been used.
